title: I built the light cycle arena I always wanted. Free, in your browser, no signup - you're on the grid in 5 seconds. Solo. Multiplayer. Casual. Competitive. Built with Claude, Codex, Meshy, Suno and ElevenLabs.
author: Amoner
selftext:
Available: [https://photonecycles.com/](https://photonecycles.com/)

24/7 Radio: [https://photonecycles.com/radio](https://photonecycles.com/radio)  
  
This has been my labor of love of the past 2-3 years. Idea itself been in my head ever since SC2 custom map "Photoncycles", to make it into a standalone mode.   
  
Started with a 2D version that was not that much different from Snake in JS and a browser. Managed to get a multiplayer version hosted and play with friends. This was done with Anthropic's early models and copy-pasting code.    
  
Then I went ambitious and tried Switching over to Unity, managed to make a single player experience that resembled what you can see now in the game, but had challenges with # of wall segments being spawned and optimizing for that. Then I went to Unreal Engine and got to the same bottleneck. Took a break from the project for a little bit and then came back to build it in UEFA, with idea that maybe it can have legs as a custom map for fortnite. Didn't really get far there...  
  
Went the full circle back to the browser and the biggest breakthrough came with Opus 4.6 where things started clicking together. Three.js, Node + AWS GameLift got the framework up and running for the full multiplayer experience. And been using 5.6 Sol, Fable, Opus for the final leg here with polish. 

For aesthetics, I have been using ChatGPT to generate visual of how I envision things and then use Meshy to make the models, and then Claude with Blender MCP for animations (Still some work to get done there). 

For music, I ended up using Claude to design the "universe" of music, and then used Suno to generate all of the songs, eleven labs to generate voices of DJs, ADs, and Public Safety Announcements to make it more "alive" and then used Codex to implement a real-time, globally synced up radio. 

The gameplay is all server authoritative with predictions. 5 different arenas, time synced up with CST to provide different levels of ambiance. Implemented both the wall latching and rubber mechanics from other games of the same genre. The goal is to make it a community-voted on development and add more casual content. 

Photone//Cycles 2.0 will be work on dedicated clients for each platform. Steam, iOS, Android, Web and etc..  Backend should stay as is, that part actually is modern and can evolve to support all of those.  

My thought on this is to take it as far as I can myself, and if it was ever to become successful, I could hire actual artists and designers to remake everything with human touch in mind.

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: The game certainly could use polish in a lot of areas, however, the game cycle, with curving lines instead of only 90 degrees like the original make an interesting play and it get's the blood pumping when you are about to get cut off or sandwiched between lines. As Disney is famously a bit sensitive with its IP, I'd say make a theme of your own. It's fun.

replies.author: Amoner
replies.body: Agree! Any specific areas you would prioritize first?

replies.author: johnesco
replies.body:
I HAD GREEN AGAINST THE WALL! RED CAME IN AND JACKED MY BLOCK! DID YOU SEE MY TURN AND ....  \*ahem\*

Would not be sure where to start, the gameplay feels nice. The UI and instructions I feel need to read better but personally I'd ignore visuals until you had the gameplay physics locked down. The turn radius feels really nice, good lean. Opponents feel competent but not impossible. It's a great sourdough starter and can't wait to see where else it goes.
